recon.notes: WordPress + The Events Calendar (Tribe) confirmed by a working /wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events endpoint. Three doors agree on exactly 2 upcoming events (REST total=2, ICS 2 VEVENTs, listing "2 évènements found."). No recurring series anywhere: no `series` key on REST rows, no RRULE in the ICS, no tribe_event_series post type, no series REST route. The site geo-detects the visitor's country and rewrites prices into EUR ("Nous avons mis à jour nos prix à Euro") — the curl-fetched pages show "25.00€ – 35.00€" and EUR ticket tiers (16/22 and 16/19/22) while REST cost_details says CAD 25–35; cover below is taken from REST (CAD). traps.label: Header strip card "EVENEMENT 06 SEP. Bar Le Dimant Rouge Montréal" (THE HUNT, 2026-09-06)
traps.why: The site-wide header strip on /events/ (and every page) still features THE HUNT four days after it happened, linking to the WordPress page /the-hunt/ rather than the Tribe event. It is not an upcoming event: REST upcoming total is 2 and the listing says "2 évènements found.". It IS in the past archive ("septembre 6 @ 21 h 00 min - septembre 7 @ 3 h 00 min", Bar Le Dimant Rouge). Extraction is correct behaviour under the global config.allowPastEvents: true — but it must be dated 2026-09-06, never re-dated forward.

traps.label: "Évènements précédents" past view — 12 + 1 past events (Kink! Playground 2025-08-02 … THE HUNT 2026-09-06)

traps.label: Currency banner: "Nous avons mis à jour nos prix à Euro pour faciliter votre processus d'achat."
traps.why: The WooCommerce currency switcher geo-detects the visitor ("Espagne" from this fetch) and rewrites every displayed price into EUR while keeping the same digits for the summary range ("25.00€ – 35.00€") — so a scrape from a non-Canadian IP reads a wrong currency. The authoritative cover is REST cost_details (currency_code CAD, values 25–35). Not an event; a data-quality hazard for the cover field.

openQuestions.q: PLAYERS start time: the Tribe listing/JSON-LD/ICS all say 21:00 ("octobre 3 @ 21 h 00 min"), but the flyer reads "SAMEDI 3 OCTOBRE - 22H À TARD". Recorded as 21:00 (site wall-clock); which does the promoter mean?

The WordPress site timezone is a fixed UTC-4 offset (REST timezone "UTC-4", ICS TZID=America/Halifax). Both current events fall in EDT so the wall-clock is right, but any event dated after 2026-11-01 (EST) will carry a -04:00 offset in JSON-LD/ICS that is one hour off Montreal — the scraper should trust the displayed wall-clock + city timezone, not the offset.
